Overview

Pactrail converts a proposed transaction and observable wallet behavior into safeguards an application can enforce. A policy response contains a decision, an agreement template, parameters and human-readable reasons.

Current release: the public API runs in deterministic demo mode. The adapter boundary is ready for Nansen Profiler data once NANSEN_API_KEY is configured.

Quickstart

Send a JSON request to the policy endpoint:

curl -X POST https://pactrail.vercel.app/api/policies/evaluate \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "actor": "0x71A9...2F18",
    "counterparty": "0x3C42...91E7",
    "amount_usd": 10000,
    "intent": "service_payment"
  }'

Data modes

Demo mode

Deterministic fixtures make development and judging reliable. Wallet suffixes map to contrasting behavioral profiles; no external calls are made.

Live mode

The production adapter will normalize Nansen transactions, balances, related wallets, counterparties and DeFi positions into the same internal feature schema.

Evaluate a policy

POST /api/policies/evaluate

  • actor — wallet initiating the transaction
  • counterparty — wallet receiving or fulfilling it
  • amount_usd — proposed agreement value
  • intent — service_payment, dao_grant, marketplace or agent_purchase
  • risk_tolerance — conservative, balanced or permissive

Decision model

Pactrail returns one of four decisions:

  • ALLOW — no additional controls recommended.
  • ALLOW_WITH_SAFEGUARDS — continue using the returned agreement terms.
  • REVIEW — require a human or independent resolver.
  • DENY — policy constraints prohibit execution.

Explainable signals

Every control is traceable to a specific observation. Pactrail never emits a permanent universal wallet score. Signals are scoped to the proposed transaction and expire with the policy response.

{
  "code": "DEAL_SIZE_ANOMALY",
  "severity": "high",
  "observation": "Value is 3.4× the largest observed receipt",
  "control": "FULL_ESCROW_FUNDING"
}
